message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the **federal holidays that create “official” long‑weekends** in Canada for 2023 (i.e., holidays falling on a Friday or Monday, giving you a three‑day break without needing to take extra time off):

| Date | Holiday | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Feb 20** | Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba) | Monday | Sat – Sun – Mon |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | Friday | Fri – Sat – Sun |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | Monday | Sat – Sun – Mon |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | Monday | Sat – Sun – Mon |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | Monday | Sat – Sun – Mon |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas Day | Monday | Sat – Sun – Mon |

> **Note:**  
> - New Year’s Day (Jan 1) fell on a Sunday, Canada Day (Jul 1) on a Saturday, Remembrance Day (Nov 11) on a Thursday, and Boxing Day (Dec 26) on a Tuesday. These don’t automatically give you a three‑day weekend unless you take an extra day off.  
> - Some provinces observe additional holidays that can create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in NL, Heritage Day in BC, etc.). If you’re targeting a specific province, let me know and I can add those too.
